'''June Chan''' (born June 6, 1956) is an American [[lesbian]] activist and [[biologist]]. As the organizer and co-founder of the Asian Lesbians of the East Coast (ALOEC), Chan raised awareness for [[LGBTQ]] issues relating to the [[Asian Americans|Asian American]] community.

== Biography ==
Chan was born on June 6, 1956, in [[Lower Manhattan]] to parents who worked in [[Chinatown, Manhattan|New York City's Chinatown]].{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=32}} Chan's mother was a refugee from the [[Second Sino-Japanese War|Japanese invasion of China]].{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=33}} Chan attended the [[Bronx High School of Science]] and graduated in 1973.{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=32}} She went on to earn her [[bachelor's degree]] in [[biology]] at the [[City College of New York]] in 1977.{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=32}} Chan earned her [[master's degree]] in biology from the [[University at Buffalo|State University of New York at Buffalo]].{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=32}} After graduate school, she [[Coming out|came out]] to her family, which was a mostly positive experience.{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=32}} Chan also works in research on [[Neuroscience|neurobiology]].{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=32}}

Chan and Katherine Hall met in 1983 and began working on projects together. They created a [[slide show]] of Asian lesbians in history and literature which was presented in the 1980s.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hfr7Us7PhGkC&pg=PA162|title=Daring to Find Our Names: The Search for Lesbigay Library History|last=Carmichael Jr.|first=James Vinson|publisher=Praeger|year=1998|isbn=978-0313299636|page=162}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Wilkinson |first=Willie |title=Out, Loud, and Seen: The Asian and Pacific Islander Lesbian and Bisexual Women's Movement Past and Present |url=https://www.cla.purdue.edu/waaw/corinne/Wilkinson.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023232242/http://www.cla.purdue.edu/WAAW/corinne/Wilkinson.htm |archive-date=23 October 2013 |access-date= |website=Women Artists of the American West}}</ref> Their slide show was considered "grassroots scholarship" by Polly Thistlethwaite.{{Sfn|Thistlethwaite|1998|p=3}}

Also in 1983, Chan and Hall formed the Asian Lesbians of the East Coast (ALOEC) in response to the overly white and male demographics of the [[LGBTQ|LGBT]] community at the time.{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=32}} ALOEC conducted workshops and published newsletters.<ref name=":0" /> ALOEC took part in the [[Second National March on Washington for Lesbian and Gay Rights]].{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=33}} During the process of organizing the march, Chan connected with other Asian-American lesbian groups.{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=33}} These groups and ALOEC formed the Asian Pacific Lesbian Network (later called the Asian Pacific Bi-Sexual Lesbian Network).{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=33}} In 1994, ALOEC participated in the 25th commemoration of the [[Stonewall riots]].{{Sfn|Henry|1995|p=33}}
